title: claimproof.basis/v0 durable claim export
description: One recorded completion claim, the content fingerprints it was measured against, and WHICH version of WHICH repository those fingerprints belong to. Produced by ClaimBasis.export(). Deliberately NOT produced by capture.receipt: that line is same-turn and session-local, it has no candidate and never did, and binding it would make it outlive the only question it can honestly answer.

producer.description: Who wrote this. Present so a reader never has to infer it.

state.description: RE-MEASURED at export time, never read back from the store. UNKNOWN is a real answer and is never folded into HOLDS: a reader must be able to tell 'I checked and it holds' from 'I could not check'.

evidence.description: Content fingerprints, not content. The raw text is deliberately never stored: this store gets committed, and evidence is often a log line.

digest.description: sha256 truncated to 16 hex chars, or '<absent>'.

candidate.description: The binding. Without it an export is a digest with nowhere to point.

identity.description: OPAQUE ON PURPOSE. A git commit is the common case and not the only one: a dirty working tree, a generated snapshot and a container digest are all real candidates. A consumer must not require 40 hex characters.

identity_kind.description: What sort of thing `identity` is, so a reader decides what it may do with it instead of guessing from its shape. Known today: git-commit, git-commit-dirty, opaque.
